segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And I'm Erika.
segments.zh: 我叫 Erika。

segments.en: And today we're bringing you part two of the presidential farewell speech of President Eisenhower.
segments.zh: 今天，我们将为您带来艾森豪威尔总统的总统告别演讲的第二部分。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, we saw in a previous lesson the beginning of this speech.
segments.zh: 所以，我们在上一课中看到了这次演讲的开始。

segments.en: Now we're going to look towards the end of the speech.
segments.zh: 现在我们将着眼于演讲结束。

segments.en: Now, we must tell you as well that we did change the speech a little bit, right?
segments.zh: 现在，我们也必须告诉你，我们确实稍微改变了演讲，对吧？

segments.en: We changed it a little bit to make it a little bit more comprehensible and also we did shorten it.
segments.zh: 我们稍微改变了它以使其更易于理解，并且我们确实缩短了它。

segments.en: We didn't make it this short.
segments.zh: 我们没有做到这么短。

segments.en: We did take out a lot of stuff.
segments.zh: 我们确实拿出了很多东西。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, again, Marco, why are we looking at this speech?
segments.zh: 所以，再一次，马可，我们为什么要看这次演讲？

segments.en: What are we learning from it?
segments.zh: 我们从中学到了什么？

segments.en: Well, in this last part of the presidential farewell speech, there are a lot of great words that are more difficult and very poetic.
segments.zh: 好吧，在总统告别演讲的最后一部分中，有很多很棒的词更难，更有诗意。

segments.en: So you can use them in different formal circumstances or just to sound a little bit more well-spoken.
segments.zh: 因此，您可以在不同的正式环境中使用它们，或者只是听起来更有说服力。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And we also, again, are going to look at some really quite difficult and challenging structures that we hope you can use maybe when you're giving a formal talk or even in your writing if you want to sound quite professional.
segments.zh: 同样，我们还将研究一些非常困难和具有挑战性的结构，我们希望您可以在进行正式演讲时甚至在写作中使用它们，如果您想听起来很专业的话，甚至可以在写作中使用。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So, why don't we listen to the dialogue for the first time?
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不第一次听对话呢？

segments.en: Let's listen how President Eisenhower says goodbye and then we'll come back and look at the words.
segments.zh: 让我们听听艾森豪威尔总统如何说再见，然后我们会回来看看这些词。

segments.en: We now stand ten years past the midpoint of a century that has witnessed four major wars among great nations.
segments.zh: 如今，我们已经跨过本世纪中点十年；这个世纪见证了大国之间的四场重大战争。

segments.en: Three of these involved our own country.
segments.zh: 其中三场，我们的国家也参与了。

segments.en: Despite the carnage of these conflicts, America is today the strongest, the most influential, and the most productive nation in the world.
segments.zh: 尽管这些冲突造成了惨重伤亡，今天的美国仍是世界上最强大、最有影响力、生产力最高的国家。

segments.en: We are understandably proud of this preeminence, yet we realize that America's leadership and prestige depend not merely upon our unmatched material progress, riches, and military strength, but on how we use our power in the interests of world peace and human betterment.
segments.zh: 我们有理由为这种领先地位感到自豪，但也明白，美国的领导地位与声望，不仅取决于无与伦比的物质进步、财富和军事实力，还取决于我们如何运用力量，促进世界和平与人类福祉。

segments.en: Throughout America's adventure in free government, such basic purposes have been to keep the peace, to foster progress and human achievement, and to enhance liberty, dignity, and integrity among peoples and among nations.
segments.zh: 美国探索自由政府的历程始终以这些为根本目标：维护和平，促进进步和人类成就，增进各国人民与国家的自由、尊严和完整。

segments.en: We pray that peoples of all faiths, all races, all nations may have their great human needs satisfied, that those now denied opportunity shall come to enjoy it to the full, that all who yearn for freedom may experience its spiritual blessings, that those who have freedom will understand also its heavy responsibilities, that all who are insensitive to the needs of others will learn charity, that the scourges of poverty, disease, and ignorance will be made to disappear from the earth, and that in the goodness of time, all peoples will come to live together in a peace guaranteed by the binding force of mutual respect and love.
segments.zh: 我们祈愿，各种信仰、各个种族、所有国家的人民都能满足基本需求；如今被剥夺机会的人能够充分获得机会；所有渴望自由的人都能享受其精神恩泽；已经拥有自由的人也能理解其沉重责任；漠视他人需要的人学会仁爱；贫困、疾病和无知的灾祸从地球上消失；终有一天，所有人都能在相互尊重与爱的维系下和平共处。

segments.en: Now, on Friday noon, I am to become a private citizen.
segments.zh: 本周五中午，我将重新成为一名普通公民。

segments.en: I am proud to do so.
segments.zh: 我很自豪能这样做。

segments.en: I look forward to it.
segments.zh: 我很期待。

segments.en: Thank you and good night.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，晚安。

segments.en: Well, that certainly was a very moving speech, hey?
segments.zh: 好吧，那肯定是一个非常感人的演讲，嘿？

segments.en: Very moving and to a certain point, a little bit religious, huh?
segments.zh: 非常感人，到了某种程度，有点虔诚，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, I think we'll talk a little bit about that a little bit later, but let's concentrate on the language now.
segments.zh: 是的，我想我们稍后会谈一谈，但现在让我们专注于语言。

segments.en: So we'll go to Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以我们会去语言外卖。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: All right, on Language Takeaway today, we'll start with our first word and it's preeminence.
segments.zh: 好吧，关于今天的语言外卖，我们将从我们的第一个词开始，它的卓越地位。

segments.en: All right, we are understandably proud of this preeminence.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为这种卓越而感到自豪是可以理解的。

segments.en: A preeminence.
segments.zh: 卓越。

segments.en: So preeminence, what is this?
segments.zh: 那么卓越，这是什么？

segments.en: Basically, it's the state of being the leader of something.
segments.zh: 基本上，这是成为某物领导者的状态。

segments.en: Okay, so in this case, America was the preeminent nation.
segments.zh: 好吧，在这种情况下，美国是最重要的国家。

segments.en: Right, so they were coming up, they were very prosperous, so they had a preeminence in the world.
segments.zh: 是的，所以他们来了，他们非常繁荣，所以他们在世界上占有一席之地。

segments.en: All right, so I think we can see here, you can use this as an adjective, a preeminent nation, or as a noun, an uncountable noun, the preeminence of our state.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我想我们可以在这里看到，您可以将其用作形容词、杰出的国家或名词、不可数名词、我们国家的卓越地位。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Since we can use this word as a noun and an adjective, why don't we listen to some more examples so we can get a better understanding of it?
segments.zh: 既然我们可以将这个词用作名词和形容词，为什么我们不听更多的例子，以便我们可以更好地理解它？

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: Now, please welcome Dr. Frank Hicks, the world's most preeminent expert on nuclear biology.
segments.zh: 现在，请欢迎世界上最杰出的核生物学专家弗兰克·希克斯博士。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: He's been a leader in his field for 25 years and his preeminence has never been questioned.
segments.zh: 25年来，他一直是该领域的领导者，他的卓越地位从未受到质疑。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: Carol Dixon is one of the most preeminent experts in green technology.
segments.zh: Carol Dixon 是最杰出的绿色技术专家之一。

segments.en: All right, well, Eisenhower was talking about all of the things that the American people had done since they became a free nation, and one of these things was to foster progress in human achievement.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，艾森豪威尔在谈论美国人民自成为一个自由国家以来所做的所有事情，其中一件事是促进人类成就的进步。

segments.en: Foster progress in human achievement.
segments.zh: 促进人类成就的进步。

segments.en: Well, I like this verb a lot, to foster something.
segments.zh: 好吧，我非常喜欢这个动词，来培养一些东西。

segments.en: So if I say to foster progress or to foster something, what am I saying?
segments.zh: 因此，如果我说要促进进步或培养某些东西，我在说什么？

segments.en: To help something grow and develop.
segments.zh: 帮助某事成长和发展。

segments.en: To take care of it, to nurse it.
segments.zh: 照顾它，照顾它。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And we commonly hear this word associated with children, right?
segments.zh: 我们经常听到与儿童有关的这个词，对吧？

segments.en: A foster child.
segments.zh: 一个寄养的孩子。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So what's that?
segments.zh: 那是什么？

segments.en: If you have a foster child, you are basically taking care of a child because the parents can't look after them.
segments.zh: 如果你有一个寄养孩子，你基本上是在照顾孩子，因为父母不能照顾他们。

segments.en: It's not like adopting because you don't actually, it's not actually legal.
segments.zh: 这不像收养，因为你实际上没有，它实际上并不合法。

segments.en: It's just that you're helping somebody out by raising this child.
segments.zh: 只是你通过抚养这个孩子来帮助别人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So we can see the connection there, a foster child to foster something.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以看到那里的联系，一个寄养的孩子来培养一些东西。

segments.en: But you know, this is really a great word and I think it would help to give a couple of examples of how we could use it.
segments.zh: 但你知道，这真的是一个很好的词，我认为举几个例子说明我们如何使用它会有所帮助。

segments.en: So for example, I can say, our company is looking to foster better creativity in the workplace.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，我可以说，我们公司正在寻求在工作场所培养更好的创造力。

segments.en: Or we could say, here at Praxis Language, we foster the development of your English.
segments.zh: 或者我们可以说，在 Praxis Language，我们促进了您的英语发展。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So the word foster.
segments.zh: 所以福斯特这个词。

segments.en: Now moving on, in his speech, he was talking about nations and faiths and different types of groups and he said, all who yearn for freedom.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，在他的演讲中，他谈论的是国家和信仰以及不同类型的群体，他说，所有渴望自由的人。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: This is a great phrase.
segments.zh: 这个短语很实用。

segments.en: All who yearn for freedom.
segments.zh: 所有渴望自由的人。

segments.en: To yearn.
segments.zh: 向往。

segments.en: So to yearn for something.
segments.zh: 所以渴望某事。

segments.en: Now if I yearn for freedom or I yearn for something, it's basically that I really want it in my heart.
segments.zh: 现在，如果我渴望自由或渴望某事，那基本上是我真的想要它在我心中。

segments.en: Yeah, you really wish for it in a way that's almost, almost painful.
segments.zh: 是的，你真的希望它几乎是痛苦的。

segments.en: You know, you want it so badly.
segments.zh: 你知道，你非常想要它。

segments.en: Now you wouldn't say like, I'm yearning for ice cream, would you?
segments.zh: 现在你不会说，我渴望冰淇淋，你呢？

segments.en: No, unless you were locked up in prison and hadn't had ice cream for 55 years.
segments.zh: 不，除非你被关在监狱里，55 年没有吃过冰淇淋。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's usually related to something that's very difficult to get or something like freedom or yearning for.
segments.zh: 所以它通常与非常难以获得的东西或自由或渴望之类的东西有关。

segments.en: That's really important.
segments.zh: 这真的很重要。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Something very important.
segments.zh: 非常重要的东西。

segments.en: And now for our last word, President Eisenhower was talking about charity.
segments.zh: 现在，我们的最后一句话，艾森豪威尔总统正在谈论慈善事业。

segments.en: He was talking about freedom and he mentioned the scourges of poverty.
segments.zh: 他在谈论自由，他提到了贫困的祸害。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So scourges.
segments.zh: 所以祸害。

segments.en: The scourges of poverty.
segments.zh: 贫穷的祸害。

segments.en: Scourges is a really difficult but interesting word.
segments.zh: Scourges 是一个非常困难但有趣的词。

segments.en: So why don't we hear a few more examples to help us understand it.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听更多的例子来帮助我们理解它。

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: Malaria is a disease that continues to be a scourge to the developing world.
segments.zh: 疟疾是一种继续成为发展中国家的祸害的疾病。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: One day we hope to eliminate the scourge of cancer.
segments.zh: 有一天，我们希望消除癌症的祸害。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: NATO promises to wipe out the scourge of terrorism.
segments.zh: 北约承诺消灭恐怖主义的祸害。

segments.en: So as we can see, the scourges of something basically is the cause of pain or suffering.
segments.zh: 正如我们所看到的，某物的祸害基本上是痛苦或痛苦的原因。

segments.en: So now relating it back to the text, we see scourges of poverty.
segments.zh: 因此，现在将其与文本联系起来，我们看到了贫困的祸害。

segments.en: Yeah, scourges of poverty, scourges of disease, and scourges of ignorance.
segments.zh: 是的，贫穷的祸害，疾病的祸害和无知的祸害。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we can see that poverty, ignorance, and disease cause a lot of really terrible things, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们可以看到贫穷、无知和疾病会导致很多非常可怕的事情，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that's why we say they are scourges.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么我们说它们是天灾。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So scourges.
segments.zh: 所以祸害。

segments.en: So that brings us to the end of our words for takeaway today.
segments.zh: 所以这让我们今天的外卖结束了。

segments.en: But as we talked about earlier, we've got some really difficult and interesting structures to look at now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 但正如我们之前讨论的那样，我们现在在 Fluency Builder 中有一些非常困难和有趣的结构要看。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So in Fluency Builder, we'll start off with the very first sentence of the paragraph.
segments.zh: 所以在 Fluency Builder 中，我们将从段落的第一句话开始。

segments.en: When he said, we now stand 10 years past the midpoint of a century.
segments.zh: 当他说，我们现在已经过了一个世纪的中点 10 年。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I love this phrase.
segments.zh: 所以我喜欢这句话。

segments.en: We now stand 10 years past the midpoint of the century.
segments.zh: 我们现在已经过了本世纪中点的 10 年。

segments.en: Now it's interesting because he is making reference to the future in the present.
segments.zh: 现在很有趣，因为他正在参考现在的未来。

segments.en: And he's using a great phrase to do that.
segments.zh: 他正在使用一个很好的短语来做到这一点。

segments.en: We now stand.
segments.zh: 我们现在站着。

segments.en: Now we can change it a little bit and use the first part, we now stand in different circumstances.
segments.zh: 现在我们可以稍微改变一下并使用第一部分，我们现在站在不同的情况下。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to a couple of examples.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听几个例子。

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: We now stand before you to declare our love and be united in marriage.
segments.zh: 我们现在站在你面前宣布我们的爱并团结在婚姻中。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: I stand before this court and declare my innocence.
segments.zh: 我站在这个法庭面前宣布我是无辜的。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: Together we now stand before this great challenge and we will fight arm in arm to defeat poverty.
segments.zh: 我们现在一起站在这个巨大的挑战面前，我们将手挽手战斗以战胜贫困。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you can see that this is a wonderful phrase to use maybe in a formal speech, right?
segments.zh: 所以你可以看到这是一个很好的短语，也许在正式演讲中可以使用，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or a wedding again or a formal ceremony.
segments.zh: 或再次举行婚礼或正式仪式。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, and it gives you this idea, this sort of very poetic image of people sort of almost standing at the cliff, standing before the, you know, some big change that's about to take place.
segments.zh: 所以，它给了你这个想法，这种非常诗意的人几乎站在悬崖边，站在即将发生的重大变化面前。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So 10 years past the midpoint of a century, the United States has witnessed four major wars, right?
segments.zh: 那么在一个世纪的中点过去了 10 年，美国已经见证了四场重大战争，对吧？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, he said, despite the carnage of these conflicts, America is today the strongest, the most influential and most productive nation in the world.
segments.zh: 好吧，他说，尽管发生了这些冲突的大屠杀，美国今天是世界上最强大、最有影响力和最有生产力的国家。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a great, great, great structure here.
segments.zh: 这里是一个伟大的，伟大的，伟大的结构。

segments.en: Despite the carnage of these conflicts, America today is the strongest blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
segments.zh: 尽管发生了这些冲突的大屠杀，但今天的美国是最强烈的废话、废话、废话、废话、废话、废话、废话。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Now, let's look at that first word, despite the carnage of these conflicts.
segments.zh: 现在，尽管发生了这些冲突的大屠杀，但让我们看看第一个词。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, carnage, what's that?
segments.zh: 那么，大屠杀，那是什么？

segments.en: Carnage is like a massacre, right?
segments.zh: 大屠杀就像一场大屠杀，对吧？

segments.en: Where many people got hurt or killed.
segments.zh: 许多人受伤或被杀的地方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a pretty violent situation when a lot of people died.
segments.zh: 所以当很多人死亡时，情况相当暴力。

segments.en: And now why does he use this word despite?
segments.zh: 现在他为什么要使用这个词？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he's basically saying even though we had all of this death and violence in this century, we're still the greatest nation, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
segments.zh: 所以他基本上是在说，尽管我们在本世纪经历了所有这些死亡和暴力，但我们仍然是最伟大的国家，等等，等等，等等，等等，等等。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: That's exactly it.
segments.zh: 正是如此。

segments.en: I can say, for example, despite the economic crisis the world is going through, our company has an enormous opportunity to grow and be more profitable.
segments.zh: 例如，我可以说，尽管世界正在经历经济危机，但我们公司有一个巨大的发展机会，更有利可图。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or if we want to take it and imagine we're at a wedding, we might say something like this.
segments.zh: 或者，如果我们想接受它并想象我们正在参加婚礼，我们可能会说这样的话。

segments.en: You could say, despite the many difficulties this couple has faced, they have a very bright and happy future together.
segments.zh: 你可以说，尽管这对夫妇面临许多困难，但他们在一起有一个非常光明和幸福的未来。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And now if we take a look at the last paragraph, it's very interesting because it's one sentence.
segments.zh: 现在，如果我们看一下最后一段，这很有趣，因为它是一句话。

segments.en: It's a really long sentence.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常长的句子。

segments.en: It's a very long sentence.
segments.zh: 这是一个很长的句子。

segments.en: So even though it's not a phrase, let's take a look at the punctuation of this paragraph.
segments.zh: 所以即使它不是一个短语，让我们来看看这一段的标点符号。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So Eisenhower starts out by saying, we pray that peoples of all face, all races, all nations may have their great human needs satisfied.
segments.zh: 所以艾森豪威尔首先说，我们祈祷所有的民族、所有种族、所有国家都能满足他们的伟大人类需求。

segments.en: And then we have a semicolon there, right?
segments.zh: 然后我们有一个分号，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So why do we have a semicolon?
segments.zh: 那么为什么我们有分号呢？

segments.en: Well, here's what he's doing.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是他正在做的事情。

segments.en: He's saying we pray for something.
segments.zh: 他说我们为某事祈祷。

segments.en: And then he's listing the many different things that he's praying for.
segments.zh: 然后他列出了他祈祷的许多不同的东西。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's basically a list.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是一个列表。

segments.en: Yep.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we know that when you're writing a list, we commonly use commas between all the things that are in this list.
segments.zh: 所以我们知道，当您编写列表时，我们通常在列表中的所有内容之间使用逗号。

segments.en: But here, because they are long and complex ideas, a comma is not enough.
segments.zh: 但在这里，因为它们是冗长而复杂的想法，所以逗号是不够的。

segments.en: You need a semicolon.
segments.zh: 你需要一个分号。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we can see here from the text that the semicolon is a great way to separate ideas, big ideas, complex ideas in a list.
segments.zh: 因此，我们可以从文本中看到分号是将想法、大想法和复杂想法分开的好方法。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can use it and not necessarily have to end your sentence or that each idea become one sentence.
segments.zh: 所以你可以使用它，而不一定要结束你的句子，或者每个想法都变成一个句子。

segments.en: You can all just make it one big sentence.
segments.zh: 你们都可以把它变成一大句话。

segments.en: Yep.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You know, and actually I remember back to high school, Marco, my teacher told me, hey, if you throw in a few semicolons into your writing and do it properly, you'll really impress people.
segments.zh: 你知道，实际上我记得回到高中，马可，我的老师告诉我，嘿，如果你在你的写作中投入了一些分号并正确地做，你真的会给人留下深刻印象。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is good advice that you can take and throw in a couple of semicolons, a little bit of commas here and there, and it'll look like you really know how to write.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的建议，你可以在这里和那里拿几个分号，一些逗号，看起来你真的会写。

segments.en: Yep.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So with that in mind, why don't we listen to what Eisenhower wrote one last time.
segments.zh: 所以考虑到这一点，我们为什么不听艾森豪威尔上次写的一篇。

segments.en: We now stand 10 years past the midpoint of a century that has witnessed four major wars among great nations.
segments.zh: 我们现在已经过了一个世纪中点的 10 年，这个世纪见证了大国之间的四次重大战争。

segments.en: Three of these involved our own country.
segments.zh: 其中三场，我们的国家也参与了。

segments.en: Despite the carnage of these conflicts, America is today the strongest, the most influential and the most productive nation in the world.
segments.zh: 尽管发生了这些冲突的大屠杀，美国今天是世界上最强大、最有影响力和最有成效的国家。

segments.en: We are understandably proud of this preeminence, yet we realize that America's leadership and prestige depend not merely upon our unmatched material progress, riches and military strength, but on how we use our power in the interests of world peace and human betterment.
segments.zh: 我们为这种卓越的地位感到自豪，但我们意识到美国的领导力和声望不仅取决于我们无与伦比的物质进步、财富和军事实力，还取决于我们如何利用我们的力量来实现世界和平和人类的改善。

segments.en: Throughout America's adventure in free government, such basic purposes have been to keep the peace, to foster progress and human achievement, and to enhance liberty, dignity, and integrity among peoples and among nations.
segments.zh: 美国探索自由政府的历程始终以这些为根本目标：维护和平，促进进步和人类成就，增进各国人民与国家的自由、尊严和完整。

segments.en: We pray that peoples of all faiths, all races, all nations may have their great human needs satisfied, that those now denied opportunity shall come to enjoy it to the full, that all who yearn for freedom may experience its spiritual blessings, that those who have freedom will understand also its heavy responsibilities, that all who are insensitive to the needs of others will learn charity, that the scourges of poverty, disease, and ignorance will be made to disappear from the earth, and that in the goodness of time, all peoples will come to live together in a peace guaranteed by the binding force of mutual respect and love.
segments.zh: 我们祈愿，各种信仰、各个种族、所有国家的人民都能满足基本需求；如今被剥夺机会的人能够充分获得机会；所有渴望自由的人都能享受其精神恩泽；已经拥有自由的人也能理解其沉重责任；漠视他人需要的人学会仁爱；贫困、疾病和无知的灾祸从地球上消失；终有一天，所有人都能在相互尊重与爱的维系下和平共处。

segments.en: Now, on Friday noon, I am to become a private citizen.
segments.zh: 本周五中午，我将重新成为一名普通公民。

segments.en: I am proud to do so.
segments.zh: 我很自豪能这样做。

segments.en: I look forward to it.
segments.zh: 我很期待。

segments.en: Thank you, and good night.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，晚安。

segments.en: All right, we're back, and we're here again with Pete, our voice actor for the second part of the dialogue.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，我们又和 Pete 在一起了，我们是对话的第二部分的配音演员。

segments.en: And Pete, we have a couple more questions for you today.
segments.zh: 还有皮特，我们今天还有几个问题要问你。

segments.en: Cool.
segments.zh: 好啊。

segments.en: So I hear in Eisenhower's speech that he keeps referencing God.
segments.zh: 所以我在艾森豪威尔的演讲中听到他一直在引用上帝。

segments.en: Like he keeps saying, I pray, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
segments.zh: 就像他一直说的那样，我祈祷，抱怨，废话，废话，废话，废话。

segments.en: He said God's speed, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
segments.zh: 他说上帝的速度，废话，废话，废话，废话，废话。

segments.en: So what's up with that?
segments.zh: 那么这是怎么回事？

segments.en: Why is he talking about God?
segments.zh: 他为什么要谈论上帝？

segments.en: Well, this is a very interesting question.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常有趣的问题。

segments.en: Traditionally, America has had a really clear boundary between church and state.
segments.zh: 传统上，美国在教会和国家之间有着非常明确的界限。

segments.en: And you'll hear a lot of rhetoric these days that says, you know, we're a Christian nation, and we were founded as a Christian nation.
segments.zh: 这些天你会听到很多言辞，他们说，你知道，我们是一个基督教国家，我们是作为一个基督教国家而成立的。

segments.en: Well, that's baloney.
segments.zh: 嗯，这就是巴洛尼。

segments.en: Baloney, so it's not true.
segments.zh: 巴洛尼，所以这不是真的。

segments.en: At the time when the country was founded 200 years ago, it was overwhelmingly Christian.
segments.zh: 在这个国家成立 200 年前的时候，它绝大多数是基督徒。

segments.en: If the founding fathers, as we call them, like George Washington and them, if they had wanted a Christian nation, they could have had it.
segments.zh: 如果开国元勋，如我们所说的，就像乔治华盛顿和他们一样，如果他们想要一个基督教国家，他们本可以拥有它。

segments.en: They explicitly did not.
segments.zh: 他们明确没有。

segments.en: And a lot of people since then have gotten that confused.
segments.zh: 从那时起，很多人都感到困惑。

segments.en: And now when we have a very large Muslim population, we have Buddhists, we have, you know, people in all various different kinds of, you know, Mormonism and everything, it's even less possible now.
segments.zh: 而现在，当我们有大量的穆斯林人口时，我们有佛教徒，我们有，你知道的，各种各样的人，你知道的，摩门教和一切，现在变得更不可能了。

segments.en: So I'm kind of baffled when I hear people say that America is a Christian nation.
segments.zh: 所以当我听到人们说美国是一个基督教国家时，我有点困惑。

segments.en: But you even have it now in the coins, like, or on the money, right?
segments.zh: 但是你现在甚至在硬币上或钱上都有它，对吧？

segments.en: It says in God we trust.
segments.zh: 它说我们相信上帝。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That started in the early 20th century.
segments.zh: 这始于 20 世纪初。

segments.en: I think that was Teddy Roosevelt era.
segments.zh: 我认为那是泰迪罗斯福时代。

segments.en: He opposed that.
segments.zh: 他反对。

segments.en: Roosevelt was really opposed to that, but...
segments.zh: 罗斯福真的反对，但是...

segments.en: And then what happened?
segments.zh: 然后发生了什么？

segments.en: They approved it.
segments.zh: 他们批准了它。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And, you know, people said later, like Eisenhower talking about this stuff, you know, in America we have something called the Pledge of Allegiance, which I don't think you guys probably have.
segments.zh: 而且，你知道，人们后来说，就像艾森豪威尔谈论这些东西一样，你知道，在美国，我们有一种叫做效忠誓言的东西，我认为你们可能没有。

segments.en: Not in Canada.
segments.zh: 不在加拿大。

segments.en: Obviously, you wouldn't do it to America, but to your own.
segments.zh: 显然，你不会对美国这样做，而是对你自己的。

segments.en: It's kind of...
segments.zh: 它有点...

segments.en: Like a salute to the flag, right?
segments.zh: 就像向国旗致敬，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, it's a little bit nationalist.
segments.zh: 是的，有点民族主义。

segments.en: I did it growing up.
segments.zh: 我是在成长的过程中做到的。

segments.en: You put your hand over your heart and you face the flag and you say, I pledge allegiance to the flag of the United States of America and to the republic for which it stands, one nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.
segments.zh: 你把手放在心上，面对国旗，你说，我宣誓效忠于美利坚合众国的国旗和它所代表的共和国，一个国家在上帝之下，不可分割，人人享有自由和正义。

segments.en: That part about one nation under God, that was added in the 50s as a kind of a way of showing that America is not, quote unquote, a godless communist country.
segments.zh: 关于上帝在上帝之下的那部分，在 50 年代被添加为一种表明美国不是引用 unquote 的方式，这是一个无神论的共产主义国家。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Yeah, because communism teaches, you know, no religion.
segments.zh: 是的，因为共产主义教导，你知道，没有宗教。

segments.en: And so they, make sure we're not communist.
segments.zh: 所以他们，确保我们不是共产主义者。

segments.en: Okay, but we don't think that, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，但我们不这么认为，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I mean, I'm all about tolerance.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，我完全是关于宽容的。

segments.en: So I think that's kind of absurd.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这有点荒谬。

segments.en: Okay, so what I think is really interesting, though, is that every political speech, every time a political leader has to say something publicly, he'll always quote God, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为真正有趣的是，每次政治演讲，每次政治领袖都必须公开说些什么，他总是会引用上帝的话，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And they'll often end a speech with, you know, thank you and God bless America or something.
segments.zh: 他们经常会以，你知道，谢谢你，上帝保佑美国之类的东西来结束演讲。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: Which, you know what, for me as a Canadian is really strange.
segments.zh: 哪个，你知道吗，对我作为加拿大人来说真的很奇怪。

segments.en: Like if a Canadian president said, God bless Canada, everyone would, no one would know what to do.
segments.zh: 就像一位加拿大总统说，上帝保佑加拿大，每个人都会，没有人会知道该怎么做。

segments.en: Like, I don't know.
segments.zh: 喜欢，我不知道。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: Anyway, I had an ex-girlfriend who was British and she, like Tony Blair started with that a couple times.
segments.zh: 无论如何，我有一个英国的前女友，她和托尼·布莱尔一样开始了几次。

segments.en: He said, you know, and God bless us all or something.
segments.zh: 他说，你知道，上帝保佑我们所有人什么的。

segments.en: And she was just put off by it.
segments.zh: 她只是被它推迟了。

segments.en: And she was like, the Brits will never take this.
segments.zh: 她就像，英国人永远不会接受这个。

segments.en: And they didn't.
segments.zh: 他们没有。

segments.en: No one was impressed.
segments.zh: 没有人印象深刻。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, an interesting feature of American history, politics and society.
segments.zh: 嗯，美国历史、政治和社会的一个有趣特征。

segments.en: So thanks for that insight, Pete.
segments.zh: 所以谢谢你的洞察力，皮特。

segments.en: Cool.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: My pleasure.
segments.zh: 我的荣幸。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And if you guys have any comments or any suggestions about this lesson or any upcoming lessons, just let us know.
segments.zh: 如果你们对本课或任何即将上课的课程有任何意见或任何建议，请告诉我们。

segments.en: Or American politics in general.
segments.zh: 或一般的美国政治。

segments.en: I'll try to stop in on the forum and see if I can answer a question or two.
segments.zh: 我会尝试在论坛上停下来，看看我是否可以回答一两个问题。

segments.en: That would be awesome.
segments.zh: 那会很棒。

segments.en: So visit us at EnglishPod.com and Marco, myself and Pete are around to answer your questions.
segments.zh: 因此，请访问 englishpod.com 和 Marco，我和 Pete 随时为您解答您的问题。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Thanks for downloading and goodbye.
segments.zh: 感谢您的下载和再见。
